                    ### Question
                    A 37-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being attacked with a knife. Physical examination shows a 4-cm laceration in the midline of the right forearm. An MRI of the right arm shows damage to a nerve that runs between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles. Loss of sensation over which of the following areas is most likely in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Palmar surface of the little finger
opb. Lateral aspect of the forearm
opc. Fingertip of the index finger
opd. Medial aspect of the forearm
ope. Dorsum of the thumb

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Injury to the nerve between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles can lead to damage to the median nerve. This damage typically results in loss of sensation in the palmar surface of the thumb, index, and middle fingers, rather than the little finger. Therefore, the most likely area of loss of sensation in this patient would be the fingertip of the index finger (opc). Evidence paths confirm the relationship between the median nerve and sensation in the fingers, supporting this conclusion.
